apps.versionDescription:
On the Usage page, scrolling ends at the usage cards.
Settings now has a Data section. "Clear Cached Usage" removes the stored usage numbers but keeps your accounts and sign-ins, then loads fresh usage right away.
"Delete All Local Data" in the new Data section removes every account and saved sign-in, groups, alert settings, usage history and app settings from the device, after you confirm. Your provider accounts are not affected and other linked devices keep their own copies.
A new Usage page charts how much of each account's weekly limit you used on each of the last 7 or 30 days, on a percent scale that steps by 5, 10 or 20 percent to fit the busiest day, with a dashed line at every weekly reset on the 30-day view. Days when the app was not refreshing show as missing instead of zero, partly estimated days are marked, and accounts without a weekly limit say so. An account with only a monthly limit, such as ChatGPT Free, shows its monthly usage on the 30-day view. History builds up from the next refresh onward.
On phones and narrow windows, a bottom bar switches between Usage, Accounts and Settings, so the Settings button is no longer in the sidebar. On wider windows, Usage, Accounts and Settings sit together at the bottom of the sidebar, above the sync status, and Ctrl+U opens Usage while Ctrl+A opens Accounts (⌘U and ⌘A on macOS). Ctrl+A no longer opens the Add Account dialog; Ctrl+N still does.
"Clear Usage History" in Settings now removes the recorded daily usage while keeping your accounts, sign-ins and current usage.
On Antigravity account cards, the Gemini 4 Argon limit is labeled Argon.
On the Usage page, the Today label under the 7-day chart and the weekly reset dashes on the 30-day chart use the same purple as the current page link.
The Settings shortcut (Ctrl+, or ⌘,) now returns to the page you opened Settings from, such as Usage, instead of always going back to Accounts.
